title: Memento
events_chronological: Insurance investigator Leonard Shelby interviews claimant Sammy Jankis and rules his memory loss psychosomatic, denying the claim.
Sammy's diabetic wife tests him by asking for injection after injection, and dies of the overdose he cannot remember giving her.
Intruders attack Leonard and his wife in their bathroom; Leonard kills one and is struck in the head, losing the ability to form new memories.
Leonard builds a system of Polaroids, annotated notes and tattoos to hunt the second attacker, a man he knows only as John G.
About a year before the main action, the cop Teddy helps Leonard find and kill the real John G., a killing Leonard forgets within minutes.
In a motel room he cannot remember checking into, Leonard narrates the Sammy Jankis case down the phone to an anonymous caller.
Leonard burns his wife's hairbrush and books in a field, trying to grieve a loss he can never retain.
The caller feeds Leonard a name and location, identifying the drug dealer Jimmy Grantz as John G.
Leonard beats and strangles Jimmy in a derelict basement and photographs the body.
As he dies Jimmy whispers "Sammy", which Leonard cannot explain, and Leonard changes into the dead man's suit and takes his Jaguar.
Teddy arrives and tells Leonard that Jimmy was innocent, that Leonard already avenged his wife a year ago, and that Leonard is himself the man in the Sammy Jankis story.
Rather than believe him, Leonard burns the photographs of Jimmy, writes "don't believe his lies" on Teddy's picture and copies down Teddy's licence plate as his next John G.
Leonard drives to a tattoo parlour and has the plate inked on his thigh as Fact Six.
At her bar, Jimmy's girlfriend Natalie recognises the dead man's clothes and car and serves Leonard a beer the staff have spat in.
Natalie hides every pen in her house, goads Leonard into hitting her, then returns bruised and blames Dodd so that Leonard will go after him.
Leonard ambushes Dodd in a motel bathroom, beats him and drives him out of town at gunpoint.
Natalie runs the licence plate through a friend at the DMV and hands Leonard a record naming John Edward Gammell - Teddy.
Leonard lures Teddy to the derelict building, shoots him in the head and photographs the corpse.
syuzhet_notes: Two threads alternate. The colour scenes - told-order bullets 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 14-18 - run in reverse chronological order, each beginning where the previous one started. The black-and-white motel scenes - told-order bullets 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 13 - run forward. The two threads meet at told-order bullet 14, when the film turns to colour mid-scene and then plays forward to the end. Told-order bullets 4, 6 and 10 are flashbacks to before Leonard's injury.
fabula_notes: The first killing of the real John G. is asserted by Teddy and glimpsed only as a single image of Leonard lying beside his wife with a fresh tattoo. The film deliberately leaves undecided whether the Sammy Jankis material is a case Leonard investigated or a displaced account of his own wife's death, so the chronological placement of the first two bullets is the most defensible reading rather than a settled fact.
